σεαυτοῦ , -ῆς, also σαυτοῦ , -ῆς, Ion.
σεωυτοῦ , ῆς, reflexive Pron. of 2nd pers.,
A.of thyself, etc., in masc. and fem. of gen., dat., and acc. sg., first in Alc. 87 , Pi. Fr. 97 , Hdt. 1.45 , 108 ; ἐν σαυτοῦ ( v.l. -ῷ ) γενοῦ contain thyself, S. Ph. 950 : rarely in neut., “φίλον ξύλον, ἔγειρέ μοι σεαυτὸ καὶ γίγνου θρασύ”
E. Fr. 693
:—the Trag. use the longer form (but not so freq. as the shorter), S. Ant. 547 , OT 312 , etc.:—in pl. always separated, ὑμῶν αὐτῶν, etc.: and orig. separated in sg., as in Hom. , who always has σοὶ αὐτῷ, σ᾽ αὐτόν; and so τὰ σ᾽ αὐτοῦ, τὰ σ᾽ αὐτῆς for τὰ σά αὐτοῦ, etc., v. σός
1.3 .—The separated forms, σοῦ αὐτοῦ, αὐτοῦ σοῦ, etc., were used in Att. , not as reflexive, but as emphat. personal pronouns, cf.
Pl. Grg. 472b , A. Th. 632 .
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
